design.title: Design system
design.repoTitle: Use a file in the repository
design.noTokens: No design-tokens.json yet: the agents read the document, but the automatic QA check needs tokens. Extract again or add them in Edit.
design.tokensInvalid: The tokens are not valid JSON.
design.fontsNote: Font previews use fonts installed on this Mac.
design.qaBody: Before every QA review the app checks the lines the task added to UI files: colours outside the palette, Tailwind's default colours, radii, shadows and gradients the system doesn't have, and the banned patterns. QA also reviews screenshots against the document.

brief.productPlaceholder: A desktop app where a team of AI agents builds software from a spec…

design.chooseDirection: Three directions. Pick the one that fits; the agent then writes the full design system for it.

storybook.enableBody: Every new or changed UI component gets stories for its states, and QA screenshots them. If the project has no Storybook yet, the next UI task sets it up (it adds dev dependencies to the project).
storybook.pendingTitle: Storybook will be set up with the next UI task
storybook.pendingBody: Agents set it up in the task's branch, so it appears here after you merge that task. Then you can start it here and browse the components in your browser.

design.replaceApp: This replaces the current design system (document and tokens) once the agent finishes. Edits you made in this tab will be lost.
design.replaceRepo: This overwrites {{path}} in your repository (and design-tokens.json next to it) once the agent finishes. Commit or back up your version first if you want to keep it.

refs.title: References
refs.body: Images, brand books, token files and sites the design system should build on. Each one is looked at once when you add it; the design agent then works from those notes, so you can add as many as you like. "As is" references are rules (exact colours, fonts, brand rules); "Inspiration" ones set a direction, not a copy. They are used by "Extract", "Design a new one" and by the agents and QA.
refs.drop: Drop images, PDFs or token files
refs.sitesHint: One per line. Each is opened in a hidden window: screenshot and CSS.
refs.conflictTheme: Light references: {{light}}, dark: {{dark}}. Remove the ones that don't fit, or the agent will pick one and say why.
refs.tooMany: {{count}} inspiration references: the agent opens 6 of them and knows the rest from their notes. Many different ones blur the direction; keep the ones that matter.

apply.title: Apply to the project
apply.failed: The redesign could not be planned.
apply.found: {{findings}} places in {{files}} files don't follow the design system. Read the brief, then Analyse.
apply.checkingBody: Every UI file is compared with the system's tokens, without a model.
apply.unavailableBody: The design system has no tokens (colours, radii, fonts) to compare the code with. A redesign brief can still be planned from the document.
apply.diffTitle: The system is updated, the code is not yet
apply.diffBody: New tasks are already built by the system. The UI written before it keeps its old look. The check compared every UI file with the tokens — without a model, at no cost.
apply.cleanTitle: The code already follows the system
apply.cleanBody: The check sees colours, radii, shadows and gradients. A redesign can still rework what it can't see: layout, hierarchy, type scale and components.
apply.next1: The spec import opens with the redesign brief — you can add to it
apply.next2: The analyst splits it into tasks: the shell and shared components first, then the screens
apply.next3: You review the tasks before they are created
apply.nextNote: One analyst session; the tasks run like any others

start.title: Where to start
start.body: Pick your situation. Either way the agents build by the system and QA checks every UI change against it.
start.keepTitle: I like how it looks now
start.repoQuestion: Already keep a design system document in the repository?

stale.title_one: You added {{count}} reference after the system was written
stale.title_other: You added {{count}} references after the system was written
stale.body: The agents see their notes, but the system's rules — colours, fonts, radii — are still the old ones. For the references to change how the product looks, update the system, then apply it to the code.

keep.card: The agent writes down the visual language the code already has. New tasks keep to it.
keep.rulesHint: A brand book or a token file, if you have one. The agent takes it as exact rules: these colours and fonts, nothing else.
keep.extractHint: The agent reads the project's styles, theme and components, together with the rules above, and writes the system.

new.card: Show what you like and describe the product: the agent proposes three directions, you pick one.
new.refsHint: Sites, screenshots, a brand book you like. Each is looked at once when you add it. “Inspiration” sets a direction, not a copy; “As is” gives exact rules (colours, fonts). Switch the role on each one.
new.briefHint: Describe the product: the agent proposes three different directions from the brief and the references. Pick one and it writes the full system.
new.replaces: Choosing a direction replaces the current design system.

view.emptyBody: Set one up: extract it from the code or design a new one. It will show here.

library.body: The latest version of every wireframe and screen the tasks drew. Each task's designer starts from these and adds its own.
library.emptyBody: When a task that changes UI finishes its design, its wireframes and screens appear here.

beforeCode.title: Design before code
beforeCode.body: For a task that changes the interface, a designer agent draws its screens before the plan, on the task's Design tab. The coder builds to them and QA compares the result.

modes.offHint: Coders build from the spec and the design system
modes.wireframesHint: Structure of every screen and state, styled by the coder
modes.fullHint: Then the screens in the design system: the coder's reference

approvals.ownerHint: The task waits on its Design tab for you, at the wireframes and at the design
approvals.autoHint: The designer checks its own frames against the spec and the design system; you see them on the Design tab and in review

package.title: A ready package from a designer
package.card: A design-system package as a zip or a folder: its tokens are taken exactly, the agent writes down the rules, components are rebuilt in your code.
package.stepHint: A .zip or a folder. It is unpacked into the project's .vibe-teamlead/design/package/ folder; nothing from it is ever run.
package.chooseHint: Nothing is imported until you confirm.
package.references_one: {{count}} image or PDF added as a reference
package.references_other: {{count}} images and PDFs added as references
package.referencesSkipped_one: {{count}} more image or PDF is left out: at most {{max}} become references (each one is read by a model).
package.referencesSkipped_other: {{count}} more images and PDFs are left out: at most {{max}} become references (each one is read by a model).
package.noTokens: No tokens: the agent will extract them
package.colorsDropped_one: {{count}} colour is over the limit of {{max}} and is left out of the tokens.
package.colorsDropped_other: {{count}} colours are over the limit of {{max}} and are left out of the tokens.

themes.title: Themes
themes.body: Switching recomputes the tokens from the package; no agent runs. Tasks started afterwards follow it.
themes.lightHint: The dark values stay in the package as reference. Cheaper: QA checks one theme.
themes.lightDark: Light and dark with a switch
themes.lightDarkHint: The planner adds the switch; the designer and QA cover both themes.
